description: Review-2 challenge benchmark template. Copy to evaluation/queries_challenge.json, replace every example entry with a manually labelled query on UNSEEN videos, and delete the 'status': 'example' markers. The evaluator refuses to run while example entries remain, so template numbers can never be reported by accident.

annotation_guidelines.videos: Use videos that were not used for any model training, validation, or the Review-1 benchmark. Record the file stem as source_video_id (the evaluator matches it to the indexed original filename).
annotation_guidelines.peak_time: Scrub the player and record the single best moment to seek to, to 0.1 s precision. For speech it is the onset of the target word; for objects/actions it is the frame where the event is clearest.
annotation_guidelines.interval: start_time/end_time bound the whole event (word span, object visibility run, action duration). Do NOT snap to 5-second boundaries; the point of this benchmark is sub-segment precision.
annotation_guidelines.ambiguous: At least 15 queries with two defensible readings (spoken vs visible, action vs word, OCR vs speech). Set expected_intents to every reading that is actually present in the video; if only one reading exists, list only that one so intent accuracy is meaningful.
annotation_guidelines.timestamp: At least 15 queries whose answer is a precise moment (a word onset, an object appearing, a gesture).
annotation_guidelines.negative: At least 5 queries for things that do not occur in the video. negative=true and no relevant list.
annotation_guidelines.two_annotators: For conference use, have a second annotator label at least 20 queries independently and report agreement (Cohen's kappa on intent, mean |peak difference| on time).
annotation_guidelines.tolerance_seconds: Default 2.0. Do not lower it below the frame sampling interval of the index.
